messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: NETWORK ALERT — Detected sustained packet loss (>25%) on egress toward upstream provider BlueTransit from us-west-2 edge. Affected prefixes: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24. Starting automated diagnostic. Paging oncall.

Priya: taking — oncall-net here. Saw alerts in Console too. Can others confirm from other PoPs?

Marcus: confirming from sfo and sea. Traceroutes show hop 5-6 loss toward BTN core. Noting path variance across regions.

Lina: posting BGP status from sfo-edge:
```
BGP neighbor 198.51.200.2 (AS 64512) - Established
  prefixes received 420
  recent events: flap 2026-03-15T20:05 -> 20:07
  last reset: 00:03:22
```

Tomas: @Priya @Marcus any quick mitigation? Can we divert via alternate transit (CloudLink) and prep route withdraw for the 203.0.113.0/24 if it keeps flapping?

Priya: spinning up temporary route-maps to prefer CloudLink for those prefixes. Starting announce/withdraw script now. Will do graceful withdraw to avoid blackholing.

Marcus: pinging BlueTransit NOC (noc@bluetransit.example) and opening ticket. Sent initial packet capture and traceroute. ETA - waiting for NOC reply.

NOC-BGPNOC: Received report, already seeing flaps on our PE toward your ASN. We're triaging with backbone ops. Will post updates.

Priya: mitigation step 1: adjust local MED/weight to prefer CloudLink. Step 2: apply prefix-limit on the peer to reduce reconvergence load. Executing step 1 now.

Lina: applied weight on sfo/sea/usw edges. Traffic shift happening — egress % to CloudLink increased from ~5% -> ~72% in 30s. Packet loss on BlueTransit path dropping for some prefixes.

Marcus: continuing handoff, I'm taking the incident at 20:08 UTC. Priya handing over. @Tomas I'll coordinate network config change approvals.

Tomas: acknowledged, taking notes for post-incident report and customer-impact timeline.

Emily (CS): flagged top-10 customers that hit us-west endpoints in last hour. Prepping outbound notification template. Any ETA for full recovery?

Priya: BlueTransit NOC says they're seeing an internal peering switch fabric issue and working on hardware replacement. No firm ETA yet.

Marcus: for transparency — we've opened temporary route-sets to move active sessions off the affected transit. Impact now reduced to degraded for a small subset of prefixes (mostly 203.0.113.0/24). Will keep on-call monitoring for 30m.

NOC-BGPNOC: update — we've isolated a misconfigured aggregation causing route churn from ASN 64512. Applying fix to suppress churn. Monitoring BGP stability.

Priya: running quick validation across regions:
- sfo: BGP stable, 0% loss on critical prefixes
- sea: BGP stable, minor residual loss ~1-2% on 203.0.113.0/24
- ord: unaffected

Marcus: customers with high-sensitivity SLAs were shifted to CloudLink automatically. Emily, please share the short incident note: affected routes, mitigation (reroute to CloudLink), current status: degraded->partially mitigated.

Emily (CS): will send initial advisory to affected accounts and stand by for follow-up RCA once finalized. Thanks for quick mitigation.

Lina: leaving a snippet of the diagnostic commands used:
```
# show ip bgp neighbors 198.51.200.2
# traceroute -n -w 2 203.0.113.5
# tcpdump -i eth0 host 203.0.113.5 and not port 22 -c 100
```

Marcus: closing the active page but keeping thread open for 2h monitors. Action items: 1) follow up with BlueTransit for RCA and time-of-fix; 2) validate prefix limits and community tags; 3) postmortem to include decision timeline for reroute. Assigning owners: BlueTransit comms - Marcus; RCA draft - Tomas; Customer comms - Emily; Config review - Priya/Lina.

Priya: thanks team. Will follow up with config diffs and ensure the temporary route-maps are removed once BTN confirms stable for 1h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to P3. Automated monitors will alert if loss >5% for next 60m.

Marcus: last note — if BlueTransit doesn't provide RCA within 24h we escalate to partner ops and consider longer-term routing policy (permanent prefer CloudLink for 203.0.113.0/24).
